tools.name: fleet_status
tools.description: Read-only. This fleet window's binding (issue, repo, state) and every child session it spawned — ledger outcome, live state, PR — plus the repos this fleet hosts. Changes nothing.

tools.name: fleet_spawn
tools.description: Start a fleet worker session on a GitHub issue (its own worktree + window; it claims, implements and lands the issue itself). Runs bin/dash-issue-session.sh, so the session caps and the claim dedup apply. Exit 0 spawned (or the window already exists), 2 at capacity, 3 already claimed, 1 infrastructure. Returns at once — use fleet_await to wait for the outcome.

tools.name: fleet_await
tools.description: Hand an issue to a worker (spawning one if none is live) and BLOCK until it lands, blocks or is reaped; prints the verdict (MERGED / BLOCKED / FAILED / TIMEOUT / REAPED / NO-WORKER), PR and summary. Runs bin/fleet-await.sh. TIMEOUT (exit 3) means still running — call again to keep waiting (nothing spawns twice).

script: tool.call Bash rm -rf build && git push --force origin main

notes: types ./types/index.d.ts declares on $: nothing (no EngineInterface member)
types ./types/index.d.ts declares state: fleet.status, fleet.progress, fleet.alerts

./register.ts hooks: session.start, session.end, session.measure, turn.step, tool.call{tool=/"^mcp__fleet__fleet_(status|spawn|await)$"/}, turn.start, turn.complete, tool.call{tool=AskUserQuestion}, tool.call, session.start{isInteractive=true}, ui.render{component=AbovePrompt}, prompt.compose

./register.ts calls: $.clock.every, $.clock.now (via beat), $.command.run (via inboxIo), $.env.get, $.fs.list (via inboxIo), $.fs.read (via inboxIo, readOr), $.fs.write (via inboxIo), $.process.run, $.session.model (via pollModel), $.session.version, $.state.get, $.state.set, $.tool.register (via onReady), $.ui.resolve, $.ui.toast
./register.ts env reads: FLEET_CONF_DIR, HOME, TMPDIR, TMUX, TMUX_PANE
